S075-01.notes: Subject relative pronoun 'who' (subject of 'traveled'); 'whom' is object case, 'she' creates a comma-splice-like fused structure, 'which' is for non-persons. Facts OK: Sacagawea joined at Fort Mandan in spring 1805 and traveled to 1806 with infant Jean Baptiste.

S075-02.notes: Main verb needed for subject 'Bayard Rustin'; A, B, C leave the sentence without a finite main verb. ~250,000 and roughly two months of planning are accurate; 'chief organizer' is standard (formally deputy director under Randolph).

S075-03.notes: Colon introduces the quoted phrase after a complete clause. Semicolon needs an independent clause after; C is a comma splice; D ungrammatical. Quote widely attributed to Hamer.

S075-04.notes: Past perfect for event (1968) prior to 1972 past-tense 'became'. Others wrong tense. Facts accurate.

S075-05.notes: 'However' is an interrupter mid-clause, needs commas on both sides. D puts semicolon between 'The next year' (fragment) and rest. Thorpe stripped in January 1913 for 1909-10 minor-league pay; accurate.

S075-06.notes: Dangling modifier: subject must be Clemente, the one honored. Facts (18 seasons, 3,000 hits, Dec 31 1972 crash, 1973 special election, first Latin American inductee) accurate.

S075-07.notes: Plural subject 'findings' needs 'were'; past time frame ('until 1900') rules out 'has been'. Facts accurate (1866 publication, 1900 rediscovery).

S075-08.notes: 'the number ... is'; trap 'are' agreeing with 'copies'. Gingerich census ~276 first-edition + ~325 second-edition copies, about 600; accurate.

S075-09.notes: 'speed and exactness' -> precision. Others contradict praise. Facts fine.

S075-10.notes: Beading and rolling off = water-repellent (lotus effect). Fine.

S075-11.notes: Describes the transistor and its importance. Facts accurate (Dec 1947, Bardeen/Brattain in Shockley's group, billions on a smartphone chip).

S075-12.notes: Belief -> test -> challenging result. 2008 Prior et al. magpie study accurately described (later replication attempt failed in 2020, but passage claims only 'widely cited', which is accurate).

S075-13.notes: Gallup offers an alternative explanation (parasite-like spot response). A contradicts; B, C overstate. Facts accurate (Kohda 2019; Gallup 1970 test; Gallup's parasite critique).

S075-14.notes: Leading more when salmon is scarce suggests ecological knowledge of food. Matches Brent et al. 2015 (Current Biology).

S075-15.notes: Inside range 29-31 (2 deg) vs outside 20-35 (15 deg) directly shows stability. Computed; B, D single-point comparisons.

S075-16.notes: Fewer crystalline regions -> weaker fibers directly ties strength to crystalline regions. Fine.

S075-17.notes: Bird observation -> solving train tunnel-boom problem. 500 Series facts accurate.

S075-18.notes: Sequence 1985 -> 1987 -> 1991 calls for 'Subsequently'. Swimmer resigned to head the BIA; accurate.

flags.note: First sentence states without qualification that Argentine ants from different nests rarely fight; in their native range (Argentina) colonies are territorial and aggressive. The low-aggression behavior is characteristic of introduced populations. Consider 'In many places where they have been introduced, Argentine ants...'.

S075-19.notes: Lack of inter-nest aggression causes nests to link into a supercolony -> 'As a result'. 'Similarly' is a possible trap but second sentence is a consequence, not a parallel example.

S075-20.notes: Only A mentions both tennis and golf firsts. Notes accurate (1950 Forest Hills, 1956 French, 1957-58 Wimbledon/US, 1964 LPGA).

S075-21.notes: Dash introduces appositive explanation of infrasound. A: semicolon before non-clause; C comma splice; D 'which' leaves relative clause without verb. Payne's 1984 discovery accurate.

S075-22.notes: She saw machines were the future, so (accordingly) learned FORTRAN. Facts accurate.

S075-23.notes: Petition was a response to the segregated-school obstacle. Facts accurate (Hampton High School petition, 1958 first Black female engineer at NASA).

S075-24.notes: Only B links her model to GPS daily use. Facts accurate (1956 Dahlgren, 2018 Hall of Fame).
